actual: Clicking the 'HTTP Methods Guide' reference button inside the collapsed 'Endpoint Naming Conventions' section left the current document unchanged (correct), but no toast/prompt/inline message ever appeared in the DOM (checked via accessibility snapshot, toast-selector queries, and polling document.body.innerText for 1.5s) telling the user to expand the section first.

evidence: Selecting REST API Design Guidelines displayed title, description, module (API), date (2024-01-15), version (v2.3.0), 3 content sections, and 4 related documents.
Clicking 'REST API Design Guidelines' related-doc link from within HTTP Methods Guide document navigated to and displayed REST API Design Guidelines as the active document.
Collapsing expanded 'REST Principles' section hid its body paragraph and made its reference links non-interactive (cursor pointer removed), while section header remained clickable to reopen.
Re-expanding the collapsed 'REST Principles' section restored the body paragraph and both reference links as clickable (cursor=pointer).

REST API Design Guidelines' content sections reference API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide; related documents list the same 4 docs (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting) - none is REST API Design Guidelines itself. HTTP Methods Guide's related documents list only REST API Design Guidelines, not itself.

Expanded 'REST Principles' section chevron icon has class 'rotate-180' while collapsed sections (Endpoint Naming Conventions, Pagination & Filtering) lack that class, and icon state matches body/link visibility observed in FT-4/FT-5.
Searching for 'zzznonexistentqueryxyz' showed 'No documents found' / 'Try adjusting your search or filter criteria' message; clearing the search restored the full 20-document list.

Graph renders exactly 19 nodes matching all 19 documents across 5 modules; REST API Design Guidelines node has exactly 4 connected edges matching its 4 related documents in the document view. Reset View control brings the graph to a standard 100% view.

19 graph nodes = 19 total documents; nodes colored distinctly per module (API cyan, Authentication purple, Data Layer green, UI Components orange, Core System pink/red); 19 edges drawn, with 4 edges verified connecting to REST API Design Guidelines matching its actual related-document relationships.

Set REST API Design Guidelines doc open with REST Principles=collapsed, Endpoint Naming Conventions=collapsed, Pagination & Filtering=expanded. Switched Documents→Favorites→Documents: all three section states and selected document (h1 "REST API Design Guidelines") persisted exactly via DOM check (chevron rotate-180 class). Set graph zoom to 140% via Zoom In, switched Knowledge Graph→Documents→Knowledge Graph (no node clicks): section states remained unchanged (collapsed/collapsed/expanded), selected doc unchanged, and graph zoom read exactly "140%" on return, confirming zoom/pan and document/section state all persist across tab switches.

issue: Clicking a knowledge graph node does not open the associated document
actual: Single-clicking and double-clicking a graph node (verified via direct DOM query of svg <g class="graph-node"> elements) only visually selects/highlights the node (adds a glow circle, increases stroke-width). It does not open the document detail view, does not auto-switch to the Documents tab, and no "View Document"/"Open Document" affordance appears anywhere in the DOM after selection. Expected behavior per spec (documents and graph should be navigable/synchronized) would be for a node click to open or at least offer to open the corresponding document.
evidence: Clicked node "REST API Design Guid..." (and double-clicked as a follow-up), then queried document.querySelectorAll for any open document heading/back-button — none appeared; active nav tab remained "Knowledge Graph"; only the clicked node's circle gained a glow/stroke change.

Navigation bar contains three tab buttons: "Documents", "Knowledge Graph", "Favorites". Successfully clicked and switched between all three multiple times throughout testing; the [active] attribute correctly moves to whichever tab is clicked (e.g. Knowledge Graph shows [active] after clicking it), and each tab renders its distinct view (document list/detail, SVG graph, favorites list).

Favorited 3 docs (Accessibility Standards, API Key Management, REST API Design Guidelines) via card star buttons. Nav "Favorites" badge updated in real-time after each toggle (1→2→3), confirmed via DOM. Applied "API" module filter and changed sort to "Last Updated" — favorites count/localStorage array remained intact (3 items) and favorite star states (aria-label "Remove from favorites") were preserved on cards after clearing the filter. Dedicated Favorites tab correctly displayed exactly the 3 favorited docs spanning different modules (API, UI Components, Core System) with no module-filter restriction. After full page reload (browser_navigate to same URL), localStorage "tech-docs-storage" still contained all 3 favorites and the nav badge still read "3", confirming persistence.
